best_for: Beginners, teachers and solo developers who want to make 2D or 3D games without writing code, and who may pay later for more cloud and publishing quota.
description:
GDevelop is a game engine and editor for 2D and 3D games, made by the GDevelop team together with an open source community. Games made with it have shipped on Steam, on mobile and on the web.

You place sprites and scenery by dragging them onto the scene and see the result as you build. Tutorials and courses sit inside the app, from a beginner course for your first casual game to step-by-step guides for a platformer, a roguelike or a 3D driving and zombie game. An AI tutor answers questions as you go. Your game can also have multiplayer lobbies, leaderboards and player accounts, and exporting it for desktop, web or mobile takes one click.

points.title: Game logic without code
points.text: You build behavior with events and ready-made behaviors instead of a programming language. JavaScript is there when you want to extend it.

points.title: The engine is MIT and free
points.text: The editor and engine are open source under the MIT license. The paid plans are about online services, not the editor itself.

points.title: What the free plan includes
points.text: Free gives 3 cloud projects, 40 AI credits a month, unlimited publishing to gd.games, and one Android and one desktop build per day. There is no iOS publishing and version history lasts 2 days.

points.title: More quota costs money
points.text: Silver, Gold and Pro raise cloud projects, AI credits and daily builds. iOS publishing starts at Gold, and team sharing comes with Pro. The pricing page did not show amounts when read, so check it before you plan a budget.

points.title: Online features need an account
points.text: Cloud storage, online builds and publishing are tied to a GDevelop account. Local editing works without paying.

points.title: Frequent releases, long history here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 127 versions, with per-user and machine-wide installers. macOS ships one universal image. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub for x64 and Arm64. macOS and Linux list only the current release.
